The root cause is PROVEN offline without reconstructing protected raw bytes. For target chip profile 0x2504, the P6 parser accepted only the four-byte body 00 04 25 00 because it invented zero constraints for opaque bytes 0 and 3. SHA-256 of that sole accepted body is 85d71424865a86046b9e07a3b371a646a2b36f0c36fa5c8dceca4c712c2d5ee6, which differs from the qualified non-secret target pin 82537d2c108887baef128b47ad401fc888d54b184673b1fc23811d79ab6d5703. The legacy path has always treated CHIP_82 as an exact four-byte digest-pinned body and decodes the little-endian chip profile only from bytes 1 and 2; it never required the two opaque coordinates to be zero. P6 now reuses that boundary: exact four-byte length, supported 0x2503/0x2504 profile, preservation of all four bytes, followed by the unchanged whole-body legacy digest comparison before any secure graph.
